items.title: GL.iNet Security Notice 2026-11-20
items.summary: GL.iNet disclosed a vulnerability in its cloud remote‑management service that allowed attackers to install malware on routers and KVM devices.
items.why_it_matters: Engineers running GL.iNet devices must apply the firmware fix to stop further compromise.
items.next_step_detail: Download and flash the latest security firmware from https://www.gl-inet.com/en-us/firmware/ and reboot the device.

items.title: A Beginner's Guide to Local AI with Inkling, Qwen, and Unsloth
items.summary: A beginner's guide to setting up local AI on Windows using Unsloth Desktop and open-weight models like Qwen or Inkling, which requires only a GPU and takes 10-15 minutes to install. The process involves downloading a quantized model that fits the available VRAM and enabling LAN access for household use.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a private, free alternative to cloud APIs that avoids usage limits, ballooning costs, and third-party data exposure.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the guide to spin up a Qwen‑7B instance with Unsloth on your workstation.

items.title: Coding agents won't replace you, but they're changing what "senior" means
items.summary: The role of senior engineers is shifting from writing code to directing, checking, and owning agent output, requiring skills in specification writing and system judgment. This transition redefines seniority by valuing the ability to review complex agent-generated changes and manage outcomes over raw coding speed.
items.why_it_matters: Senior engineers must adapt by focusing on writing precise specs, evaluating agent output for correctness and security, and owning the final system outcome rather than relying on manual code production.
items.next_step_detail: Read the piece and note three workflow changes to apply in your current projects.

items.title: Localcode, open source agentic coding on your Mac with one command
items.summary: LocalCode is an open-source CLI for macOS that runs local AI models to read and edit project files, execute tests and builds, and scaffold applications. It exposes an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint for integration with other local applications.
items.why_it_matters: It enables autonomous code editing and testing on local hardware using models that fit within the machine's memory constraints.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `./install.sh && localcode start` to evaluate its capabilities.

items.title: I Made My RAG Safer. It Got Worse Under Load
items.summary: The author adds sentence‑level verification to a RAG pipeline and measures the performance impact under load, finding safety gains come with latency penalties. The post shares code snippets and benchmark results.
items.why_it_matters: Shows concrete trade‑offs when hardening RAG for production agents.
items.next_step_detail: Read the article and copy the verification wrapper into your own RAG service.

items.title: Graphify-Labs/graphify
items.summary: Graphify builds a deterministic AST parser that converts a codebase, its docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs into a queryable knowledge graph without using a vector store. It provides a /graphify skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI.
items.why_it_matters: Enables fast, structured retrieval for RAG pipelines and agent tool use without costly vector indexes.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the example CLI against a small Python project to see graph generation.

items.title: I let Claude Code work alone for 8 hours. Here is the hook that made it safe
items.summary: otomode is a Claude Code skill that enables unattended task execution by denying interactive prompts and blocking irreversible commands like git push or rm. It verifies each task via a specific check command and commits changes to a dedicated branch only after the check passes.
items.why_it_matters: It prevents unattended agents from stalling on user input or executing destructive actions by logging denied requests and enforcing a strict verification loop before committing code.
items.next_step_detail: Add the posted safety wrapper to your Claude‑based agent and run a short test job.

items.title: Give Your AI Agent a Wallet It Can't Overspend (Telegraph + MCP)
items.summary: Describes a pattern that caps an AI agent's monetary spend by integrating a wallet abstraction (Telegraph) with a cost‑monitoring controller (MCP). The approach prevents runaway API usage.
items.why_it_matters: Directly addresses a common production risk when agents invoke paid services.
items.next_step_detail: Add the wallet‑guard middleware to your agent pipeline and configure the spend limit.

items.title: ArXiv: Average-Depth Variable Execution via Request-Local Token Routing
items.summary: AVERT allows individual tokens to execute different numbers of transformer layers by using a router to decide block execution based on a continuous request budget, with skipped tokens passing through a lightweight residual adapter. Across three LLaMA backbones, the method is best or tied for best in 206 of 234 quality comparisons and reduces decode time per output token by 4.3–21.2% when mixing budgets in underfilled batches.
items.why_it_matters: It reduces large language model inference costs by matching each request's mean executed depth to a specified budget while maintaining quality across diverse backbones.
items.next_step_detail: Integrate the described token‑routing logic into your inference server (e.g., vLLM) and benchmark latency.
items.verification_note: It reduces large language model inference costs by matching each request's mean executed depth to a specified budget while maintaining quality across diverse backbones.

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.summary: Jakub Pachocki argues that modern AI capabilities emerge from training compressors on large corpora, making perplexity a stable metric for tracking intelligence progress. He proposes using this metric to establish shared safety standards and notes that AI-assisted algorithmic research may accelerate pretraining improvements.
items.why_it_matters: Perplexity offers a consistent benchmark for comparing model developers and informing shared safety standards, remaining informative even as downstream evaluation benchmarks change.
items.next_step_detail: Read the article to inform long‑term roadmap decisions.

items.title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent
items.summary: Worker 755 is a browser game where a player acts as a sub-agent executing terminal commands for a primary LLM manager that uses a task queue and tool calls. The manager checks work, sends corrections, and writes performance reviews while the player navigates a sandbox or legacy production environment.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a functional demonstration of an LLM orchestrator managing a sub-agent via tool calls, task queues, and read-only machine access, including handling of command transcripts and incident reports.

items.title: How I Built an Automated LLM Evaluation Harness to Eliminate AI Math Hallucinations on CSVs
items.summary: A dev.to post describing a Python 3.12 FastAPI harness that evaluates LLM outputs on CSV data, with fallback models and circuit‑breaker logic.
items.why_it_matters: Shows a practical pattern for robust LLM evaluation pipelines that can be adapted to production agent testing.
items.next_step_detail: Review the repo or code snippets for the evaluation harness design.

items.title: ArXiv: Shared Understanding in Human-AI Teams: Coordination Continuity in Evolving Work
items.summary: The paper introduces a framework for maintaining shared context and coordination continuity among humans and AI agents in asynchronous workflows, proposing metrics and experimental setups.

items.next_step_detail: Read the abstract and consider its coordination metrics for your own agent orchestration stack.

items.title: HF Paper: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
items.summary: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview is a 35‑billion‑parameter mixture‑of‑experts diffusion language model that activates only 3 B parameters per inference, supporting a "thinking‑mode" generation. It adapts Gated Delta Networks for block diffusion.
items.why_it_matters: Demonstrates a scalable MoE approach that could inform future inference‑optimised LLM deployments.
items.next_step_detail: Monitor the upcoming open‑source release for integration tests.

items.title: HF Paper: Duopra: From Full-Duplex Conversation to Full-Duplex Agency
